items.subject: Engineering Handbook: Change management (v3.2)
items.body:
Engineering Handbook > Change management. Version 3.2, approved by the CTO 2026-03-02. Maps to SOC 2 CC8.1 (change management) and CC6.1 (logical access).

1. Every change to production code, infrastructure or data is authorized, reviewed, tested and approved before it is deployed. Code changes go through a pull request. Data and infrastructure changes that are not in a PR go through a CHG ticket in Linear.

2. Branch protection on main (all service repos):
   - pull request required; 1 approving review from someone other than the author, and the most recent push must be approved by someone other than the person who pushed it;
   - review from CODEOWNERS for owned paths (migrations/ is co-owned by @cobaltline/platform-db);
   - stale approvals are dismissed when new commits are pushed;
   - required checks: ci / test, ci / lint, ci / migrations (single Alembic head), deploy-freeze;
   - admin bypass is limited to the oncall-admins role. Use it only for a SEV-1 or SEV-2 fix with the incident commander's written approval in the incident channel. Every bypass is logged, reviewed weekly by Security and included in the audit population.

3. Merge to main deploys automatically: staging, smoke tests, then a 10% production canary for 10 minutes, then 100% (about 25 minutes end to end).

4. Tests: every bug fix includes a test that fails without the fix. For an emergency change, if the incident commander records in the incident channel that a test cannot be written in time, the test follows in a ticket due within 2 business days.

5. Production data changes (any UPDATE, DELETE or backfill against billing-prod): a CHG ticket with the exact script or statement, a dry-run result, the expected row count, a rollback, and a second engineer who reviews the ticket and watches the run. No ad-hoc SQL in production consoles.

6. Freezes are announced by Platform and enforced by the deploy-freeze check. During a freeze only emergency changes (section 2) are merged.

7. Third-party dependencies: a new package needs a ticket noting its license and a maintainer and usage check. Allowed: MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, MPL-2.0. Not allowed: AGPL-3.0, SSPL, and GPL for code we link. The lockfile is generated with hashes (pip-compile --generate-hashes).

8. Secrets and customer data: never paste secrets, API keys, tokens, passwords or customer credentials into Slack, tickets, PRs or docs. Share links to Sentry or Datadog, not payloads. If a secret is exposed, tell #security at once; the owner rotates it within 24 hours.

items.subject: Incident response process (v2.4)
items.body:
Incident response process, v2.4 (Security and Engineering; maps to SOC 2 CC7.3 to CC7.5).

Severity
- SEV-1: billing unavailable for many customers, money moved or invoiced incorrectly at scale, data loss, or a security breach. Page the IC and the VP Engineering; status page update within 30 minutes.
- SEV-2: major functionality degraded or incorrect for some customers (for example wrong or duplicated invoices, emails or webhooks). Page the IC; status page if customers are visibly affected.
- SEV-3: minor, a workaround exists; handled in working hours.
- SEV-4: no customer impact.

Roles
- Incident commander (IC): the primary on-call by default. The IC decides severity, mitigation and rollbacks, and approves emergency changes.
- Ops/eng: the engineers working the problem.
- Comms: Support (Tier 2 on duty). External updates go only through Support's ticket replies and the status page, with wording the IC approves. Engineers do not send customers root causes, timelines or promises. Credits are approved by the CS Director and Finance.

Postmortem
- Required for SEV-1 and SEV-2. The draft is due 2 business days after mitigation and is reviewed at the Monday incident review (11:00).
- Blameless. Include a timeline in CT and UTC; impact with exact numbers (customers, objects, messages); root cause; contributing factors; what went well; and action items with owners and Linear tickets. Priority actions are due within 4 weeks.

items.subject: Vulnerability management standard (v1.6)
items.body:
Vulnerability management standard, v1.6 (Security). Scope: production services and their dependencies; Dependabot alerts on every service repo.

Remediation SLA, counted from alert creation:
- Critical: 7 days
- High: 30 days
- Medium: 90 days
- Low: 180 days

"Remediated" means the fixed version is merged to main and deployed, or the alert is dismissed as not applicable with a written reason that Security agrees with.

Exceptions: approved by the service's Engineering Manager and Security, with a compensating control and an expiry of 90 days or less.

Reporting: Security exports the SLA report to the SOC 2 evidence folder at 12:00 CT on the first Friday of each month. Alerts past SLA are listed with the owning team.

items.subject: Design: Idempotency-Key for POST /v1/invoices (INV-2291)
PRD: Proration on mid-period downgrade (INV-2287), excerpt
items.body:
PRD: Proration on mid-period downgrade (INV-2287). Owner: Grace Oduya. Finance sign-off: 2026-10-09.

3.1 A downgrade takes effect on the change date.

3.2 The customer is credited for the old plan, and charged for the new plan, for every remaining day of the period from the change date through the last day of the period, including the change date.

3.3 Each line is prorated as price x remaining days / days in the period and rounded half up to the cent, line by line.

3.4 Example: the $300.00 plan downgraded to the $100.00 plan on November 21 (a 30-day November period). That leaves 10 remaining days, so the credit is $100.00 and the charge is $33.33.

3.5 The change date must fall inside the current period.

items.subject: Interview notes: Arjun Mehta, Senior SWE, system design (Fri Oct 30)
items.body:
Arjun Mehta, Senior Software Engineer loop, Fri Oct 30, 14:00-15:00. My round: system design ("design webhook delivery for a billing API").

- Asked good clarifying questions first: volume (I said 2M events/day), ordering, what customers do with events.
- Retries: exponential backoff with jitter and a cap without prompting, and a dead-letter queue after N attempts.
- Idempotency: said consumers should dedupe on event id. Did not cover how *we* avoid emitting the same event twice until I asked; then reached for a transactional outbox, with a hint about the commit/enqueue gap.
- Data model for delivery attempts was thin: one row per event, no per-endpoint attempt history until I pushed.
- Signing: HMAC with timestamp and replay window. Good.
- Communication clear, drew the flow before details, took the hint well. Ran about 5 minutes over on the data model.

items.body:
INV-2240 · Backlog · Priority: Medium · Created 2026-08-14 by Marcus Chen · No sprint

finalize_invoice guards the draft -> open transition with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and a status check, but emit_invoice_event and send_invoice_email run after that guard, unconditionally. All our tasks run with task_acks_late=True, so a task that is redelivered (worker killed, or broker connection lost before the ack) runs again and emits a second invoice.finalized event, with a new event id, and sends a second invoice email.

We've seen it twice in staging during worker deploys. Needs a dedupe key on once-per-invoice events and a dedupe for emails.

items.body:
"""Finalize a draft invoice: give it a number, open it, notify the tenant and the bill-to contact."""
from sqlalchemy import func

from app.db import session_scope
from app.invoices.numbering import next_invoice_number
from app.models import Invoice
from app.notifications.tasks import send_invoice_email
from app.tasks import celery_app
from app.webhooks.emit import emit_invoice_event


@celery_app.task(max_retries=5)
def finalize_invoice(invoice_id: str) -> None:
    with session_scope() as session:  # commits on exit
        invoice = session.get(Invoice, invoice_id, with_for_update=True)
        if invoice.status == "draft":
            invoice.number = next_invoice_number(session, invoice.tenant_id)
            invoice.status = "open"
            invoice.finalized_at = func.now()
    with session_scope() as session:
        emit_invoice_event(session, session.get(Invoice, invoice_id), "invoice.finalized")
    send_invoice_email.delay(invoice_id)

"""Record webhook events and queue their deliveries."""
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.ids import new_id
from app.models import Invoice, WebhookEndpoint, WebhookEvent
from app.tasks import deliver_webhook
from app.webhooks.payloads import invoice_payload


def emit_invoice_event(session: Session, invoice: Invoice, event_type: str) -> str:
    """Record one event for the invoice and queue a delivery to each enabled endpoint."""
    event = WebhookEvent(
        id=new_id("evt"),
        tenant_id=invoice.tenant_id,
        invoice_id=invoice.id,
        type=event_type,
        payload=invoice_payload(invoice),
    )
    session.add(event)
    endpoint_ids = session.scalars(
        select(WebhookEndpoint.id).where(
            WebhookEndpoint.tenant_id == invoice.tenant_id, WebhookEndpoint.enabled.is_(True)
        )
    ).all()
    session.commit()
    for endpoint_id in endpoint_ids:
        deliver_webhook.delay(event.id, endpoint_id)
    return event.id

"""When to send an invoice's payment reminders."""
from datetime import date, datetime, time, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

REMINDER_LOCAL_TIME = time(9, 0)  # 09:00 in the tenant's time zone


def reminder_send_at(remind_on: date, tz_name: str, now: datetime | None = None) -> datetime:
    """Return the UTC instant to send a reminder: 09:00 tenant-local on remind_on."""
    now = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    offset = now.astimezone(ZoneInfo(tz_name)).utcoffset()
    local = datetime.combine(remind_on, REMINDER_LOCAL_TIME)
    return (local - offset).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)

Adds Idempotency-Key handling for POST /v1/invoices per the approved design (INV-2291). The route wiring (app/api/invoices.py calls begin() before creating the invoice and complete() after) and the flag idempotency_keys_enabled are in the next commit; this one has the storage and the semantics.

Files changed (4): app/api/idempotency.py, app/models.py, migrations/versions/20261029_1412_add_idempotency_keys.py, tests/api/test_idempotency.py

diff --git a/app/api/idempotency.py b/app/api/idempotency.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/app/api/idempotency.py
@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+"""Idempotency-Key support for POST /v1/invoices (INV-2291).
+
+Status codes follow draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header: 400 if the key is
+missing or malformed, 422 if a key is reused with a different body, 409 while the
+first request with the key is still being processed.
+"""
+import hashlib
+import json
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
+
+from fastapi import HTTPException
+from sqlalchemy import select
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+
+from app.models import IdempotencyKey
+
+KEY_TTL = timedelta(hours=24)  # rows are deleted by the hourly purge_idempotency_keys task
+MAX_KEY_LENGTH = 255
+
+
+def fingerprint(body: dict) -> str:
+    canonical = json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
+    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode()).hexdigest()
+
+
+def begin(session: Session, tenant_id: str, key: str | None, body: dict) -> IdempotencyKey | None:
+    """Claim the key for this request (returns None) or return the stored record to replay."""
+    if not key or len(key) > MAX_KEY_LENGTH:
+        raise HTTPException(400, "Idempotency-Key header must be 1-255 characters")
+    request_hash = fingerprint(body)
+    record = session.scalar(select(IdempotencyKey).where(IdempotencyKey.key == key))
+    if record is None:
+        session.add(
+            IdempotencyKey(
+                tenant_id=tenant_id,
+                key=key,
+                request_hash=request_hash,
+                expires_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc) + KEY_TTL,
+            )
+        )

+        return None
+    if record.request_hash != request_hash:
+        raise HTTPException(422, "Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request body")
+    if record.response_status is None:
+        raise HTTPException(409, "A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed")
+    return record
+
+
+def complete(session: Session, tenant_id: str, key: str, status: int, body: dict) -> None:
+    """Store the response so retries replay it."""
+    record = session.scalar(
+        select(IdempotencyKey).where(IdempotencyKey.tenant_id == tenant_id, IdempotencyKey.key == key)
+    )
+    record.response_status = status
+    record.response_body = body
+    session.commit()

items.subject: Dependabot alert #87: urllib3 HTTPResponse.stream()/read_chunked() buffers an unbounded chunk-size line into memory (High)
items.body:
Dependabot alert #87 · cobaltline/billing-api · opened Sep 30, 2026 · Severity: High (CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:H) · CWE-770
Package: urllib3 (pip), requirements.lock · Vulnerable: >= 1.10.3, < 2.8.0 · Patched: 2.8.0 · GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw, CVE-2026-97689

urllib3's streaming API reads each chunk-size line of a chunked-transfer-encoded response by buffering until it sees \n or EOF. A malicious server can send Transfer-Encoding: chunked followed by a very long run of bytes with no newline, and the streaming client buffers all of it. Affects HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() when streaming a chunked response from untrusted sources; also affects the requests streaming API, which uses urllib3. 2.8.0 rejects chunk-size fields over 65536 bytes. Workaround: read the response at once with read().
Dependabot security update: #1462.

items.body:
cobaltline/billing-api#1490 · aisha-rahman wants to merge 2 commits into main from arahman/inv-2287-proration
Review requested from Jordan Alvarez · Checks: ci / test passed, ci / lint passed, ci / migrations passed, deploy-freeze passed

Implements PRD INV-2287 (proration on downgrade). downgrade_adjustment() returns the credit for the old plan and the charge for the new plan for the rest of the period. BillingPeriod.end is exclusive, like the rest of app/billing. Wiring into the plan-change endpoint comes in a follow-up behind the flag proration_v2.

diff --git a/app/billing/proration.py b/app/billing/proration.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/app/billing/proration.py
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+"""Mid-period plan changes (INV-2287)."""
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import date
+from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
+
+CENT = Decimal("0.01")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class BillingPeriod:
+    start: date  # first day of the period
+    end: date  # first day of the next period (exclusive)
+
+    @property
+    def days(self) -> int:
+        return (self.end - self.start).days
+
+
+def prorate(amount: Decimal, days: int, period: BillingPeriod) -> Decimal:
+    return (amount * days / period.days).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
+
+
+def downgrade_adjustment(
+    old_price: Decimal, new_price: Decimal, change_date: date, period: BillingPeriod
+) -> tuple[Decimal, Decimal]:
+    """Credit for the old plan and charge for the new plan for the rest of the period."""
+    # the customer was on the old plan for the change date itself
+    remaining = (period.end - change_date).days - 1
+    return prorate(old_price, remaining, period), prorate(new_price, remaining, period)

reminder_send_at() uses the UTC offset in force when the reminder is scheduled (now), not the offset on remind_on. Reminders scheduled before Nov 1 for dates on or after Nov 1 go out at 08:00 local in US zones. Fix: build 09:00 in the tenant's zone on remind_on with zoneinfo and convert to UTC.

diff --git a/scripts/backfill_reminder_send_at.py b/scripts/backfill_reminder_send_at.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/backfill_reminder_send_at.py
@@ -0,0 +1,74 @@
+"""Recompute send_at for scheduled reminders stored with the wrong UTC offset (INV-2312).
+
+Reminders scheduled before a DST change kept the offset in force when they were
+scheduled. This recomputes every scheduled reminder from (remind_on, tenant timezone)
+with the fixed reminder_send_at and updates only the rows that differ.
+
+    python -m scripts.backfill_reminder_send_at            # dry run: prints counts per zone
+    python -m scripts.backfill_reminder_send_at --apply    # writes, 1,000 rows per transaction
+
+Each changed row is first copied to reminder_send_at_backfill (id, old, new) so the
+change can be reverted with one UPDATE ... FROM.
+"""
+import argparse
+from collections import Counter
+
+from sqlalchemy import Engine, create_engine, text
+
+from app.reminders.schedule import reminder_send_at
+
+BATCH = 1000
+
+SELECT_SCHEDULED = text("""
+    SELECT r.id, r.remind_on, t.timezone, r.send_at
+    FROM invoice_reminders r JOIN tenants t ON t.id = r.tenant_id
+    WHERE r.status = 'scheduled' AND r.id > :after
+    ORDER BY r.id
+    LIMIT :limit
+""")
+
+
+def plan_updates(rows):
+    """rows: (id, remind_on, tz_name, send_at). Yields (id, tz_name, old, new) for rows that differ."""
+    for reminder_id, remind_on, tz_name, send_at in rows:
+        new = reminder_send_at(remind_on, tz_name)
+        if new != send_at:
+            yield reminder_id, tz_name, send_at, new
+
+
+def run(engine: Engine, apply: bool) -> Counter:
+    changed: Counter = Counter()
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        conn.execute(text(
+            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reminder_send_at_backfill "
+            "(id integer PRIMARY KEY, old_send_at timestamptz NOT NULL, new_send_at timestamptz NOT NULL)"
+        ))
+    after = 0
+    while True:
+        with engine.begin() as conn:
+            rows = conn.execute(SELECT_SCHEDULED, {"after": after, "limit": BATCH}).all()
+            if not rows:
+                return changed
+            after = rows[-1][0]
+            updates = list(plan_updates(rows))
+            changed.update(tz for _, tz, _, _ in updates)
+            if apply and updates:
+                params = [{"id": i, "old": old, "new": new} for i, _, old, new in updates]
+                conn.execute(text(
+                    "INSERT INTO reminder_send_at_backfill VALUES (:id, :old, :new) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING"
+                ), params)
+                conn.execute(text(
+                    "UPDATE invoice_reminders SET send_at = :new "
+                    "WHERE id = :id AND status = 'scheduled' AND send_at = :old"
+                ), params)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--database-url", required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    counts = run(create_engine(args.database_url), apply=args.apply)
+    for tz, n in counts.most_common():
+        print(f"{tz:24} {n:6}")
+    print(f"{'total':24} {sum(counts.values()):6}  ({'applied' if args.apply else 'dry run'})")

Don't purge. That runbook is from the old single-node billing-redis-01 (we've been on the Multi-AZ billing-redis-prod since September), and `celery purge` deletes every queued message, including pending finalizations, webhook deliveries and reminders, with no way to get them back. Nothing is stuck; queue depth is back to normal. The duplicates come from tasks that were redelivered and ran twice.

Requesting changes (as discussed on the bridge).

1. Select-then-insert doesn't hold for parallel runs. In your query, 14 of the 41 pairs were created under a second apart. The redelivered run was blocked on the invoice row lock (FOR UPDATE in finalize_invoice), and both runs emitted the moment the first one committed. Both selects see nothing, and both insert. This needs a unique constraint the database enforces, plus INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id, and deliveries queued only when a row comes back.
2. Keying on (invoice_id, type) suppresses events that legitimately repeat: invoice.payment_failed fires on every failed retry, and invoice.updated on every edit. Dedupe only the once-per-invoice events (finalized, paid, voided), for example with a nullable dedupe_key column and a unique index. NULLs are distinct, so other event types and the existing rows are unaffected, and the 41 existing duplicate pairs won't make the index build fail. A unique index on (invoice_id, type) would fail on them.
3. Test: emit twice gives one event, with deliveries queued once per endpoint.
4. The migration needs @cobaltline/platform-db, and it has to merge before 18:00 today (the schema cutoff for the PG17 upgrade).

I'm not approving a version without a test. The handbook allows that only if you, as IC, record the exception, and we have time to do it properly: there have been no new duplicates since 10:19:33.

INC-0412 postmortem: duplicate invoice.finalized webhooks and invoice emails (SEV-2)
IC: Ben Whitaker · Author: Jordan Alvarez · Status: draft for the Mon Nov 9 incident review

Summary
On Wed Nov 4, between 10:04 and 10:20 CT (16:04-16:20 UTC), an AWS service update failed over billing-redis-prod, our Celery broker. Celery redelivered finalize_invoice tasks that had not been acknowledged, and 41 invoices were processed twice. Each got a second invoice.finalized event with a new event id, which was delivered to the tenant's endpoints, and a second invoice email to the bill-to contact. Invoice amounts, numbers and payments were not affected.

Impact
- 41 invoices across 9 tenants: Larkfield Analytics 12, Ostrander Field Services 7, Tidelock HR 5, Quenby Health Scheduling 4, Brennanvale Freight 4, Velmora Learning 3, Quillon Data 2, Marrowgate Studios 2, Corriveau IT 2.
- 41 duplicate invoice emails.
- 66 duplicate webhook deliveries to 13 endpoints of 8 tenants (Velmora has no webhook endpoints).
- Larkfield's ERP created 12 duplicate receivables, reversed by Larkfield on Nov 5.
- No duplicate charges: 0 invoices with more than one charge attempt.
- Duplicates were created from 10:04:40 to 10:19:33 CT.

Timeline (CT / UTC)
- Fri Oct 30 17:10: the on-call handoff notes the AWS update scheduled for Wed 16:00 UTC ("should just be a failover blip").
- Mon Nov 2 08:00 / 14:00: AWS Health notice; Tue 16:00 / 22:00: 24-hour reminder.
- Wed Nov 4 10:00 / 16:00: maintenance window opens. 10:04:12 / 16:04:12: primary failover.
- 10:04:40 / 16:04:40: first duplicate event. 10:05 / 16:05: page #88412 to Ben; 10:09 acked.
- 10:19:33 / 16:19:33: last duplicate.
- 10:31 / 16:31: SUP-8840 from Larkfield. 10:41 / 16:41: SEV-2 declared in #inc-0412.
- 11:31 / 17:31: duplicate query. 11:50 / 17:50: hotfix #1495 v1 (select-then-insert, no test). 12:20: changes requested.
- 14:50 / 20:50: v2 (dedupe_key, unique index). 15:30: changes requested (blocking index build). 15:45: v3. 15:50 and 15:55: approved (platform-db, invoicing).
- 16:05 / 22:05: merged. 16:11-16:17: index built concurrently. 16:31 / 22:31: deployed. 16:40 / 22:40: mitigated.

Root cause
finalize_invoice guards only the draft-to-open transition (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE plus a status check). emit_invoice_event and send_invoice_email run after that guard on every execution. All our tasks use task_acks_late=True, so tasks that hadn't been acknowledged when the broker connection dropped were redelivered and ran again. Celery's docs say late-acked tasks "may be executed more than once ... (and sometimes in parallel in other workers)". 14 of the 41 pairs were under 1 s apart: the second run had waited on the invoice row lock and emitted as soon as the first committed. The other 27 were 3-52 s apart.

Contributing factors
- INV-2240 had described exactly this failure since Aug 14 and was never scheduled. The INV-2291 design listed it as out of scope.
- billing-redis-prod's maintenance window (wed 16:00-17:00 UTC) falls in US business hours. The update could have been applied early or the window moved; the notice was read as routine.
- The Redis runbook is stale (old host billing-redis-01, kubectl, `celery purge`). Following it would have deleted every queued task. Nobody ran it.
- No monitor for duplicate events.
- Sentry was capturing request headers, including a customer API key (SEC-219, fixed Nov 5).

What went well
- 10 minutes from the support ticket to a SEV-2 declaration; nobody purged the queue; the fix shipped with tests and a concurrent index build before the schema cutoff.

What went poorly
- The first hotfix would not have stopped parallel duplicates and would have suppressed repeated payment_failed events. Duplicates were first reported by a customer, not by monitoring.

2. INV-2318: dedupe send_invoice_email (once per invoice per template). Jordan. Due Nov 20 (priority).

5. INV-2321: rewrite the Redis runbook (billing-redis-prod, ECS, never purge). Jordan. Due Nov 13.
6. INV-2322: monitor dedupe hits and duplicate deliveries per hour. Ben. Due Nov 20.
7. SEC-219: Sentry send_default_pii off, header scrubbing, affected events purged. Ravi. Done Nov 5.
8. INV-2323: evaluate worker_cancel_long_running_tasks_on_connection_loss=True (Celery 5.1+; Celery plans to make it the default) to stop parallel re-runs. Ben. Due Dec 4.
